text.p: - Russian political elite expects President Boris Yeltsin may fire Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, possibly after his March 6 address to parliament.
- If Yeltsin decides to abolish the institution of banks authorised to deal with the state budget it will ruin the sole achievement of the country's economy -- financial stabilisation.
- Russia's biggest oil companies may soon merge to create an oil giant comparable to gas monopoly Gazprom.
- The World Bank mission expressed its satisfaction with the way the so-called $500 million coal loan to Russia was spent but postponed negotiations on the next loan.
- Serious purges are expected to commence in the top military brass.
- Despite intensified speculation about the possible resignation of Viktor Chernomyrdin, President Yeltsin is unlikely to sack him because there is no real alternative.
- Plans to reshuffle the Russian government are likely to involve the economic sector of the cabinet, the paper's economic analyst says.
- In the changing geopolitical situation Russia will be playing more important role as the interests of U.S. and Germany come into conflict.
- Russia cannot afford the inefficient banking system it has now.
